why: The CLI registers per command and MCP once at import; each test boots its own surface in a fresh process, and one passing test proves only its own surface.
Each surface pins its own tool list; one passing test proves only its own surface's list.
The serializer and each writer that builds a document outside it state the version separately; one passing test proves only its own writer.
Each surface's tests walk that surface's own command or tool list; one passing test proves only its own surface leaves a 3.0 file alone.
The refusal tests and the settings.json registration test live together; the registration test is the one that goes red if the hook is unwired, and it is the only test that does not run the hook.
